close_reason: Replaced .unwrap_or("") + "" | "PartialDate" sentinel with Option<&str> match: None | Some("PartialDate") → PartialDate, Some("Timestamp") → Timestamp, Some(_) → Unknown. Behavior change: literal empty-string @type now routes to Unknown instead of PartialDate (not RFC-defined input). No test exercised that path. Pre-commit gate clean (58 tests pass). bd:JMAP-sgrr.9 (non-object asymmetry) is separate and remains open. Commit pending.
description: lib.rs:977-997 implements Deserialize for AnniversaryDate by first reading the @type tag with .unwrap_or("") and then matching on "" | "PartialDate" to mean 'PartialDate is the default'. The empty-string sentinel conflates two distinct wire conditions: (a) @type is absent (the RFC §1.3.4 default-type rule), and (b) @type is the literal empty string (which the RFC does not define). The idiomatic Rust pattern is to match on Option<&str> directly: match v.get("@type").and_then(|t| t.as_str()) { None | Some("PartialDate") => ..., Some("Timestamp") => ..., Some(_) => ... }. The Some(_) arm also lets the catch-all route any future @type into Unknown without a separate fallthrough, simplifying the relationship with JMAP-sgrr.9 (the non-object asymmetry). What goes wrong if left as-is: the sentinel pattern is unidiomatic and the empty-string arm accepts data the RFC does not describe, which is a documentation / behavior surprise for a future reader. Fix is a one-line refactor at deserialize-time; no API surface change.
title: AnniversaryDate::deserialize uses string-sentinel for missing @type — Option matching is cleaner
